newsitem.title: GREECE: SALOMON LIKES OTE, SEES CASH FLOW GROWTH.
newsitem.headline: SALOMON LIKES OTE, SEES CASH FLOW GROWTH.

text.p: Salomon Brothers maintained its buy recommendation for shares of Greek telecom OTE noting that its operating environment looked partivularly attractive relative to most other national telecoms in Europe.

"In our view the key to the company's growth is the enormous revenue benefits being gained from upgrading the local analogue network to digital and the introduction of new digital lines," Salomon said in a research report.

With strong revenue and cash flow growth, a largely protected market for the remainder of this decade and the potential to build a significant wireless business from scratch OTE's environment looked quite appealing.

"As well as allowing timed charging in the local loop for the first time, this capital investment is vastly increasing the quality of service and paving the way for the introduction of many value-added services," it said.
It saw OTE's operating cash flow growing at an average annual rate of more than 15 percent over the next three years versus an average growth of only 5.0 percent for the sector as a whole.

In addition, OTE's earnings growth -- forecast at 18 percent annually over the next three years -- suggests a substantially higher multiple than the 12 times prospective 1997 earnings on which the company is presently trading, it said.
"Despite rising almost 40 percent so far in calendar 1997, the shares continue to represent good value relative to the sector. Wireless will reinforce its revenue stream going forward," Salomon said.
The major attraction of the OTE story is that capital investment in the domestic network has an immediate and significant impact on revenues.
Network digitisation in the local loop allows the company to measure and charge for calls depending on their length for the first time.

The report which had other operators like Deutsche Telekom, Tele Denmark, Portugal Telecom, Vodafone and BT on hold said OTE remained on target to attain a digitisation rate of 80 percent by the end of the year 2000.

"In 1997, OTE is operating under an overall price cap of CPI plus 4.6 with the emphasis again on raising local rates which remain very low by European standards. Looking forward there is no formal price cap for 1998," Salomon said.
With inflation falling steadily in Greece, currently at 6.8 percent year-on-year, tariff increases would likely moderate in the future.
Last week OTE forecast 1997 pretax profit would rise 21 percent to 304 billion drachmas on revenue growth of 15 percent -- 797 billion.
Salomon sees OTE's net profit up 22 percent at 204.3 billion this year and at 242.7 billion in 1998.
OTE is seeking a strategic partner to take a 25-35 percent stake in its subsidiary set to develop the wireless business. Orange and Telenor look like the most likely candidates.
OTE shares closed down 50 drachmas on Monday, settling at 5,900.
